steps.content: She barely manages to pull Elvira into the sewer tunnel.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: We can get to an air-raid shelter from here, though it's a bit of a walk. We can set out once you've caught your breath.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Just a coincidence. Of course it is. The name isn't uncommon, but cyborgs are... Ugh, I'm so stupid...
The vibrant energy she displayed only moments before vanishes instantly, leaving in its wake an exceptionally frail figure—so thin she can barely hold up her own swaying body.

Elvira's head sinks low as her whole body seems to crumple inward, finally struck down by the immense weight of the fatigue and helplessness accumulated over the past days. She releases a long, weary sigh before she speaks, her voice reduced to a muted and hollow sound.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Ma'am, are you an Outlander?

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: I... I don't think so? My grandfather's generation settled here in Syndicate. You know how many of us there are here. So I suppose I'm a DisCity citizen now, haha.

She dares not say too much. Parfait had specifically warned her to keep a low profile before leaving, especially after Sibilla appeared on television with the investment guru, shouting those words... And conflicts have already erupted several times in the underground shelters.
...Sibilla lowers her head, realizing the lie she once told has now twisted into truth. Is this her punishment for lying as a whistle? Now she has no way to uncover what truly happened to Furor.
Elvira watches her for a long moment before speaking softly.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: But you must still hold deep feelings for your homeland.
She points to Sibilla's bracelet. Though broken and missing many beads, leaving it threadbare in places, it has been carefully restrung and clearly cherished.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: It was a gift. From my friends back home.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Could you tell me about them?

Sibilla's hesitation hangs in the air. In response, the girl across from her lowers her head, as if talking about a faraway homeland evokes many memories. For a long moment, she is silent, lost in some distant world, before she begins to speak, her voice slow and heavy with the weight of nostalgia.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Jelena</color>... That's the name my mom gave me. I grew up here in DisCity, and it wasn't until I was older that I learned it was an Outland name.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: My mom was actually an Outlander. But by the time I learned the truth... she was already gone. I never got to know her. To know about her home, her people... or how she felt, living here.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: But I want to know. Whether it's about her, or about your friends... I want to know those stories from far away. Please.
Sibilla has always held her past—the far-away stories, her dread of Furor—apart from her new life in Syndicate. How could she burden them, when they've already given her so much?
But the girl's own raw history disarms her, touching a secret, guarded corner of the Outlander's heart.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...I see. Let's find somewhere safer to talk, Miss Jelena. We have time.
